text:
Sign up for the daily Saints Newsletter by clicking here.

The New Orleans Saints officially finalized their roster after Sunday’s roster deadline and Monday’s waiver wire deadline. They can now begin preparation for their road opener against the Detroit Lions on Sept. 13.

The Saints claimed two players off waivers and finalized their practice squad Monday. Head coach Kellen Moore offered insight into the roster decisions and provided injury report updates.

Here is a notebook on everything that happened today, including Moore’s comments and our analysis.

Saints Claim Two Off of Waiver Wires

Saints executive vice president and general manager Mickey Loomis announced Monday that the club claimed offensive tackle Mason Murphy (Chicago Bears) and defensive tackle Colby Wooden (Indianapolis Colts) off waivers. To make room on the roster, New Orleans waived wide receiver Kevin Austin Jr. and tight end Treyton Welch.

Murphy was an undrafted free agent rookie who originally signed with the Chicago Bears following the 2026 NFL Draft. Murphy played in 51 career games with 34 starts throughout his college career at USC (2021-24) before finishing his career at Auburn. Murphy was picked up arguably due to his versatility as when he was at Auburn, he started the first nine games at right tackle before starting the last three at center. Given the lack of depth on the offensive line, this is a solid pickup through the waiver wire for the Saints.

Wooden played in 47 regular season games with 17 starts for the Packers (2023-25), recording 87 tackles (45 solo), 0.5 sack, nine stops for a loss, and three pass breakups. He also appeared in four postseason contests for Green Bay with one start, recording seven tackles (two solo), 0.5 sack, and four quarterback hurries. Wooden was traded to the Indianapolis Colts in March 2026 and participated in the Colts' Training Camp.

Saints Bring Back 12 Players on Practice Squad

During Moore’s press conference, the Saints released its list of the 12 players who made the practice squad.

EDGE Fadil Diggs

RB CJ Donaldson

CB TJ Hall Jr.

OT Alan Herron

OT Easton Kilty

WR Jalen Moreno-Cropper

WR Trey Palmer

LB Jackson Sirmon

K Charlie Smyth

DL Jay’Viar Suggs

RB Zamir White

OT Alex Wollschlager

Daniel Carlson Needed Just Two Days to Win the Kicking Job

Veteran Daniel Carlson secured the starting kicker role on the initial 53-man roster following successful field goal conversions of 38 and 53 yards during the Saints’ last preseason exhibition against the Dallas Cowboys. He joined the team after inconsistent performances by initial competitors Tanner Brown and Charlie Smyth led the Saints to sign him as a free agent.

“We really only had two days with Daniel, and so obviously feel like he showed himself well,” Moore said of Carlson. “Obviously made a nice kick at Dallas. And, yeah, I think more time on task was beneficial for him.”

Smyth subsequently joined the practice squad. As an Irish national participating in the International Player Pathway (IPP) program, his inclusion provides the Saints with an extra practice squad exemption. So the Saints can have 17-members on the squad instead of the normal sixteen.

Versatility Matters in Roster Decisions

Versatility likely played a major role in recent roster decisions.

One of the primary surprises was Mike Reid Jr. making the roster. Moore noted Reid's ability to play multiple positions across the defensive backfield during his press conference.

"I would say for him, he played more cornerback, nickel, and we ended up playing him a lot more at safety, and I think he did a really, really good job there," Moore said. "So we know there's versatility there. He can play in a lot of spots, but he performed excellently when he went in the back end."

The same applies to Jayden Price, a standout performer during training camp. The third-year cornerback has also excelled inside as a nickelback.

Colby Wooden, whom the Saints claimed off waivers, also demonstrated positional flexibility on the defensive line during his time with Green Bay.

Kamara, Jordan Among Key Week 1 Injury Questions

Moore addressed the challenge of navigating upcoming 53-man roster decisions amidst multiple injuries, noting that discussions are ongoing. While the team expects to place several players on injured reserve for extended periods, staff members are managing roster balance and evaluating depth options.

According to Moore, safety Lorenzo Styles has not been placed on IR. The team is weighing options, leaving open the possibility he could return within four weeks.

Regarding running back Alvin Kamara and defensive end Cameron Jordan, their statuses for Week 1 remain undetermined. Neither is expected to practice this week, with final evaluations slated for late next week.

“We'll see how this week goes,” Moore said. “We'll probably have a better idea at the end of next week. We'll have a couple practices this week, and then next week should have a good idea, obviously, of what workload those guys are able to do. And that will project us into what Week 1 looks like.”

Moore also touched on running back Devin Neal, who is navigating a recurring hamstring injury. While the injury is not more severe than his previous one, it was significant enough to land him on the season-ending injured reserve list.

“He had a hamstring injury, obviously unfortunate,” Moore said of Neal’s injury. “He's had to navigate that a couple times. And so, bummer for him because I love Dev. He's an awesome kid. And he's done a lot of good things for us.”

Saints Begin Turning the Page to Week 1

While the coaching staff is balancing final roster decisions, they have started shifting their focus toward Detroit. According to Moore, practice sessions will remain centered on internal team development alongside preliminary Detroit prep before moving into full game-week preparation next week.

text:
San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle has remained optimistic about his chances of suiting up for the team's Week 1 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia. However, nothing is certain, even days before the 49ers travel overseas.

The 49ers practiced Monday and will hold two more sessions Tuesday and Wednesday before embarking on their lengthy journey to Australia. The team will closely monitor Kittle during those practices as it evaluates whether he will be ready to play in the season opener.

NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport discussed Kittle's status during a segment on The Insiders.

"First of all, taking into account that this is an unbelievable thing that George Kittle even has a chance to play Week 1," Rapoport said. "When he tore his Achilles, I think most people were like, 'You know what? Probably going to see him in October, and that's fine. Take your time.' George Kittle does not take his time. He isn't patient. He wants to get out there and play.

"Now, he is going to take the next couple of days and really figure this out. My understanding is the 49ers truly do not know whether he is going to be able to play. They're going to push him. They're going to give him the opportunity. He has been pushing himself, but really we're going to get an answer after these couple of days of practice and not before."

Rapoport stressed that the 49ers would prefer to determine Kittle's status before traveling to Australia, potentially avoiding an unnecessary trip for the veteran tight end. That matches up with what head coach Kyle Shanahan said on Monday.

"I think if we didn't think he was going to play, and it was looking that way, I think it'd be much nicer to make that decision before we left, instead of having him go through all that," Shanahan said. "It's also a long time that we're out there, so to be away from the team for a week, not for camaraderie or anything, but just the training staff and things like that, and being away from meetings, is also a big deal, too.

"But hopefully, these three days that we have, these three practices, will go the right way, and it'll make it an easy decision to get him on the plane."

Kittle traveling with the 49ers would be an encouraging sign that the team expects its All-Pro tight end to have a chance to play against the Rams.

"We'll see if he actually does get on the plane or if he stays home if he's not able to play and just continues rehab," Rapoport added. "Either way, whether he plays in Week 1 or not, George Kittle is back sooner rather than later, and that is an incredible rehab story."

text:
Denver Broncos outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper pleaded not guilty to multiple domestic violence charges Monday in a Douglas County (Colorado) courtroom.

A trial date for Cooper was set for Nov. 10 with a jury. A pretrial hearing is set for Oct. 30.

The 28-year-old was arrested twice in a seven-day span in June on domestic violence charges, including one felony charge. Cooper was placed on the commissioner exempt list Sunday by the NFL, and he can neither practice nor play in games while he is on the list.

The list is designed to remove a player from participation in games and practices while potential violations of the NFL's personal conduct policy are reviewed. Cooper, who will be paid and can attend meetings, receive medical treatment as well as work out in the team complex while on the exempt list, could still face a league suspension.

"We continue to take this very seriously," Broncos general manager George Paton said Sunday, just after the league-wide deadline to cut rosters to 53 players. "We're going to monitor all the legal developments and continue to support Jonathon."

Cooper practiced throughout training camp and was one of the few veteran players who played in Friday night's preseason finale. Cooper played eight defensive snaps in Denver's 34-6 victory over the Minnesota Vikings.

Cooper faces a felony charge of second-degree assault by strangulation and three misdemeanors, including violating a protection order, after he was arrested June 4 and then again June 11 after incidents with his girlfriend. The felony charge stems from the first arrest after the results of a forensic examination of Cooper's girlfriend by a nurse.

The affidavit that was included in the police investigation into Cooper's first arrest included the report from the medical exam of Cooper's girlfriend. In it a nurse wrote that the woman experienced a physical injury from being choked that led to a "substantial risk of death" or substantial risk of injury, including the possibility of traumatic brain injury.

Denver coach Sean Payton has consistently deferred to the NFL's investigation and the legal process when he has discussed the team's approach with the sixth-year linebacker. Payton said the guidelines the Broncos set for Cooper after the arrest have included therapy.

On Monday, Cooper's hearing started at the same time as Denver's practice, and Payton was notified afterward about Cooper's plea and the scheduled trial date.

"We wait on the league,'' Payton said. " ... (And) we just wait for this process to play out.''

Payton confirmed Cooper will continue to participate in meetings, weight room workouts and any potential treatment for injuries as is allowed by league rules while he is on the exempt list.

Cooper was a seventh-round pick by Denver in the 2021 draft and has 31.5 sacks in 81 career games, including eight sacks last season. He has started every game in each of the past three seasons.

title: Myles Garrett 'changing the culture' of Rams, even from sideline - ESPN
authors: Sarah Barshop, Mike Reiss, Lindsey Thiry, ESPN Fantasy, Adam Schefter, Tyler Fulghum, ESPN staff, Seth Walder, NFL Nation reporters, NFL Nation
description:
MYLES GARRETT COULDN'T take part in the Los Angeles Rams' joint practice with the Dallas Cowboys in mid-August.
By trading for Garrett, the Rams added not only the NFL's best defensive player last season, but another leader on defense.
When he arrived in Los Angeles, he knew the team had an established culture, and he wasn't trying to "force" himself "on anyone or try to take over a group."
But, Rams outside linebacker Byron Young said, Garrett is absolutely "changing the culture" with the way he conducts himself.
"Playing with freedom, not being punished or critiqued for trying to make a play," Garrett said.
text:
MYLES GARRETT COULDN'T take part in the Los Angeles Rams' joint practice with the Dallas Cowboys in mid-August. But he made his presence felt.

Garrett missed that practice -- and 12 more -- as he deals with swelling in his knee.

But while Garrett wasn't practicing, he was standing on the sideline with his new teammates, vocal enough that Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott noticed.

"He was on the field," Prescott said with a smile when asked whether he was bummed he didn't get to go against Garrett in practice. "Oh, he was definitely on the field."

The Rams are being cautious with Garrett, the reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year who had a league single-season high 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns in 2025. The Rams traded for Garrett in June as part of their attempt to maximize the remaining time quarterback Matthew Stafford wants to play.

By trading for Garrett, the Rams added not only the NFL's best defensive player last season, but another leader on defense. When he arrived in Los Angeles, he knew the team had an established culture, and he wasn't trying to "force" himself "on anyone or try to take over a group."

"This group was doing great without me," Garrett said. "I want to just try to help elevate other guys and the playmakers that we have here."

But, Rams outside linebacker Byron Young said, Garrett is absolutely "changing the culture" with the way he conducts himself.

"We were about to leave yesterday and he said, 'We're not going to break it down?'" Young said early in training camp. "I was like, 'We're breaking down in the meeting room?' And he said, 'Yeah, we're going to break it down in here.' So I said, 'OK!' That's a piece of the culture that he's bringing in."

ALTHOUGH GARRETT HASN'T practiced since early August, he did start training camp on the field with the Rams. And it didn't take long for him to stand out.

"He's an alien," Rams safety Kam Curl said. "He can do whatever he wants to do, and the offense can't do anything about it. I can't wait to get to play with him on Sundays."

Safety Quentin Lake said that when watching film of practice, it's Garrett's athleticism that stands out. Lake joked, "It honestly made me feel like I'm not athletic looking at how athletic he is."

"We saw him come off the edge [in the meeting room], and I'm like, 'Man, these offenses are going to have a tough time throwing the ball,'" Lake said. "Incredible player."

Young said it didn't take him long to notice Garrett's "first step."

"When he gets off the ball, if you see him go every rep, he gets about three or four yards the first step," Young said. "That right there alone is amazing. Watching him play and practice and his mindset of getting off the ball, that's something I want to work on and be better at."

Defensive tackle Kobie Turner said watching Garrett reminded him of playing with defensive tackle Aaron Donald. The pair played one season together before Donald retired in March 2024. Donald re-signed with the Rams Sunday and was on the field for a jog-thru that afternoon. Defensive end Braden Fiske agreed, saying, "not all men are created equal, that's for sure."

"There are some things that he can do that nobody else can really do," Turner said. "There are some things that Myles can do that nobody else can really do. I've been able to appreciate some of the simplicity of a lot of his rushes. He's just beating you off the snap. He's getting to his rip and then he's able to work at the top of the rush. He works at the top of the rush really well. He's able to bend corners."

And while his defensive teammates have seen how Garrett's game will help theirs, his teammates on offense have seen how he wrecks games.

"I'm happy I'm getting to go against him in camp and not in the regular season," Rams tight end Tyler Higbee said. "He's not out there embarrassing me on national TV."

Added right guard Kevin Dotson: "I feel like for the offensive line, it's 'AD' [Donald] protocol. Wherever he is, we're going to him. We need hands on deck with him, and him having that type of effect on the offense can change the whole game plan."

And if Donald decides to come out of retirement, as he is contemplating?

"Now you have nowhere to deny what's about to happen," Dotson said. "So it'd be great."

Stafford said he remembers playing against Garrett in 2023, and going against him in practice reminded him of how challenging that can be.

"Every single play it is a chess matchup," Stafford said. "'OK, where is he? Can we run the play that we're going to run or can we not?' And then he affects every time you drop back to throw the football, right? And shoot, hand it off and run it as well."

Added Lake: "There's no question whether he's going to dominate or not. So now it's just making sure, 'Hey, can we do our job so this guy can go cut it loose over there, too?'"

THE RAMS ARE still getting to "learn" Garrett's body, McVay said, as the training staff is "establishing trust and rapport."

"He's tough as hell and he wants to be out there," McVay said when asked about Garrett's knee injury. On Aug. 25, McVay said Garrett has not suffered any setbacks with his knee and that the Rams are erring on the side of caution with the goal of getting him to peak when Los Angeles opens against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1 in Melbourne, Australia (8:35 p.m. ET, Netflix).

On the day in mid-August when McVay first said Garrett was missing practice because of swelling in his knee, he said the pass rusher told him he's feeling about 85% healthy.

"I don't know what 100% is going to look like, but it must be pretty good if that's 85%," McVay said.

Although he hasn't been on the field for much of camp, Garrett said, "it's been a joy" to be in Los Angeles with his new team. Garrett, the 2017 No. 1 pick by the Browns, said the Rams' coaching staff has allowed him to play more freely during practice.

"Playing with freedom, not being punished or critiqued for trying to make a play," Garrett said. "There are guidelines and boundaries you've got to stay within the defense, but as long as we put ourselves in the right spots, they're all for it."

Stafford has familiarity with arriving to the Rams late in his career. The veteran quarterback, now entering his 18th NFL season, was traded to Los Angeles in 2021 after spending the first 12 years of his career with the Detroit Lions. Stafford said he has "been in those shoes before, a little bit," noting, "I didn't have the pedigree that he had coming in that he has right now."

"But he's done a great job of just figuring out what we're about, understanding how we go about things, and fitting right in," Stafford said. "I mean, it's hard not to when you're as good a player as he is."

text:
Following initial 53-man roster cutdowns, NFL teams continued adjusting their active rosters through waiver claims, injury designations and more Monday.

The Dallas Cowboys made a surprise roster move in their quarterback room by waiving Joe Milton, leaving Sam Howell as the backup to Dak Prescott despite Milton's preseason performances. Meanwhile, the Washington Commanders placed left tackle Laremy Tunsil on injured reserve Monday.

More NFC East news dropped as New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers stayed noncommittal about his Week 1 availability. And the Los Angeles Chargers made headlines by reuniting the Herbert brothers.

Here is the latest from around the league on Monday:

With Week 1 right around the corner, the Dallas Cowboys made a surprising roster move on Monday morning.

The Cowboys are waiving quarterback Joe Milton to make room for running back Emari Demercado, according to ESPN. The decision clears the path for Sam Howell to serve as Dak Prescott's backup quarterback to start the season.

Milton was drafted in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft by the New England Patriots out of Tennessee.

Milton spent six years in college playing for both Michigan and Tennessee, but only started one full season during his redshirt senior year. With the Volunteers, Milton completed 64.5% of his passes for 2,813 yards with 20 touchdowns and five interceptions.

Now with Milton’s NFL future up in the air, it will be worth keeping an eye on whether another team claims him off waivers. A player with his physical tools might not stay a free agent long and could find his way into a quarterback competition sooner rather than later.

The Washington Commanders took a major roster hit on Monday afternoon. They’re placing five-time Pro Bowl offensive tackle Laremy Tunsil and defensive lineman Jer’Zhan Newton on injured reserve, according to ESPN.

Both players could return later this season, but Tunsil faces a long recovery after tearing his triceps early in training camp. Newton faces a similar uphill battle after suffering a torn pectoral muscle during a preseason game against the Miami Dolphins.

Tunsil played in 14 games last season for the Commanders after an offseason trade with the Houston Texans that brought in a true pass protector for quarterback Jayden Daniels. For a team repeatedly plagued by injuries, this season doesn’t appear to be any different.

Missing Tunsil and Newton for most or even all of the 2026 season puts head coach Dan Quinn in a tough spot in a crowded and competitive NFC East. The Commanders are set to kick off their season on the road in Week 1 against the Philadelphia Eagles.

New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers progressed from individual drills to full-contact team sessions at practice on Monday, shedding his no-contact jersey.

However, with New York set to open its regular season against the Dallas Cowboys on Sept. 13, the wideout remains uncertain if he will be cleared in time as he recovers from a torn ACL in his right knee.

"My mind is focused on playing the regular season: playing whenever that is," Nabers said after practice Monday. "There’s still some things that you still have to check off the box for you to participate. I’m still going through that, still listening to the trainers, still listening to doctors and sharing everything with them."

Nabers added that he feels "real good" physically, but emphasized that final clearance remains a process between himself, doctors, and the coaching staff.

"That’ll be a decision that will be made when that time comes," Nabers said regarding Week 1. "There’s certain things that, as a football player, you’ve got to mentally prepare (for) before you go into a game... I want to be able to come out there and make no mistakes and just be able to fly around and do what I do. I’m getting there, for sure."

The Los Angeles Chargers signed tight end Patrick Herbert to their practice squad Monday, joining his brother, starting quarterback Justin Herbert, according to NFL Network.

Patrick Herbert was waived by the Jacksonville Jaguars ahead of Sunday's 53-man roster deadline and chose Los Angeles after receiving interest from multiple teams.

The Herbert brothers previously played together at Oregon during the 2019 season, helping lead the Ducks to a Rose Bowl victory.

Patrick, who recorded two catches for 12 yards during Jacksonville's 2026 preseason action, joins a Chargers tight end group featuring Charlie Kolar, Oronde Gadsden, and David Njoku.

The Chargers open the regular season on Sept. 13 against the Arizona Cardinals.

description:

text:
WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. — Although Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald did not practice Monday, head coach Sean McVay said it was part of the team's plan for him as Donald gets re-acclimated.

Donald, who participated in individual drills but not team drills in his first practice with the team Sunday, did work in the weight room while the team was on the practice field Monday.

"Aaron not being out there was part of the plan all along, so that was kind of par for the course," McVay said.

McVay also made sure to emphasize, similar to the sentiments with Donald making a decision to return to Los Angeles, that they are still taking things "day-by-day." Going day-by-day also includes the possibility that Donald may or may not play in Australia against the 49ers on Sept. 10.

"I wouldn't rule anything out yet," McVay said when asked about Donald playing in Australia. "Sometimes when you put unnecessary parameters or guidelines on something, you can skew things. But what I think what's really good for us is if he's able to go, great, if not, that's kind of how we've been operating as is, and guys have done an excellent job of being able to do some really cool stuff in the meantime. So, if he's not ready, and that's not what's best for him and for the team, (we) absolutely wouldn't have him play in Australia."

McVay also gave an update on defensive end Myles Garrett who is still not participating in individual or team drills, stressing the importance of making sure he's available against the 49ers in Australia.

"He's making really good progress," McVay said. "Like we said, (the) goal along has been Australia, and he's doing a lot of stuff outside of what you guys see. Looking forward to getting him back out there."

On Monday's practice, tight end Terrance Ferguson and inside linebacker Grant Stuard also did not participate in practice aside from working with trainers off to the side. Similar to Garrett, McVay emphasized erring on the side of caution due to having three off days following Monday.

"Those guys, were just really erring on the side of caution, and knowing that we've got these (next) three days off," McVay said of Ferguson and Stuard's condition, with Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday off days. "They were a little bit sore, and so we were being smart with them."

McVay also addressed the placement of Keagen Trost (hamstring) and Justin Dedich (hand) on Injured Reserve and said both offensive linemen are "doing really good." The decision to place them on IR also coincided with the confidence McVay and the coaching staff have in the depth of the offensive line room.

"We felt like there was some guys that were more than capable of really earning the roster spot," McVay said. "Those guys (Trost and Dedich) will be ready to work and we'll look forward to be able to start their clock when we can, but that won't be for a little bit of time. But in the meantime, we feel good about the depth that we've been able to establish up front, especially you got your five guys that are your starters, but then to be able to have four guys you feel good about behind with David Quessenberry and Beaux Limmer done a really nice job where (Limmer) can really play all the spots on the inside. Dylan McMahon's gotten a bunch of reps at center, and then Bill Murray came in and truly earned a roster spot with the way that he played in the preseason games and the way he competed in practice."

text:
San Francisco 49ers star defensive end Nick Bosa will return to the practice field this week and is still on track to play in the season opener in Australia despite missing nearly a month with tendinitis in his surgically repaired right knee.

Bosa and tight end George Kittle, who is working back from a torn Achilles tendon, will be ramped up this week with the goal of playing in Week 1, coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday. General manager John Lynch said Bosa is following a plan that the team believes will have him ready to face the Los Angeles Rams on Sept. 10 in Melbourne (Sept. 11 local time). The coach and GM sounded optimistic, though noncommittal, about Kittle’s availability as well.

Bosa was absent from Monday’s practice, but the 49ers also have sessions on Tuesday and Wednesday.

Bosa, who turns 29 in October, last practiced Aug. 3. He is recovering from a torn ACL suffered in September, which kept him out of all but three games of the 2025 season. It was his third ACL surgery and his second on his right knee, dating back to high school. Lynch said Bosa’s experience recovering from the injury has helped the team be more patient this summer.

“Nick’s been through this before with ACLs. Nick’s pretty blessed with tremendous genes and was going along great,” Lynch said. “When he upped the activity, he got sore, so he backed off, and we put together a really good plan that we believe will have him ready for Australia.

“I always believe that the athlete knows their body better than anyone, and Nick certainly takes that to the nth degree. He knows his body extremely well.”

Including Bosa, the 49ers kept only four defensive ends on their initial 53-man roster as the cutdown deadline passed Sunday: Keion White, Sam Okuayinonu and third-round rookie Romello Height. Veteran Ogbo Okoronkwo was added to the practice squad Monday, and he could be a candidate to be elevated and play early in the season.

Mykel Williams, the 49ers’ first-round pick in 2025, must sit out at least the first four games after being placed on the reserve/physically unable to perform list. He is recovering from his own torn ACL, suffered in November. Lynch said the team wanted to give him additional time to recover because he also had cartilage damage.

Kittle, who tore his Achilles in January and turns 33 in October, was activated from the physically unable to perform list Aug. 23. Two weeks ago, he said he had a chance to face the Rams in the opener but acknowledged he wouldn’t put the rest of the season at risk to rush back for Week 1.

Kittle said if he doesn’t face the Rams, he would prefer not to travel to Australia so he could focus on his rehab. The 49ers will fly out Wednesday evening and arrive in Melbourne on Friday morning. Shanahan said the team would prefer to decide before the flight but doesn’t necessarily have to.

“It’d be much nicer to make that decision before we left,” the coach said. “Hopefully these three practices will go the right way and make it an easy decision to put him on the plane.”

The 49ers kept four tight ends on the initial roster, though one of them, Brayden Willis, is recovering from a concussion.

Other news and notes

• The team re-signed safety Ashtyn Davis and punter Corliss Waitman and placed cornerback Nate Hobbs (groin) and linebacker Nick Martin (hamstring) on injured reserve, ruling them out for at least four games each.

• The 49ers also brought veteran long snapper Jon Weeks back to the practice squad. He can be promoted for three games before he must be signed back to the active roster.

• Shanahan said the 49ers haven’t decided on a starting left guard yet, saying, “It’s fluid.” It appears the team could be going with the element of surprise ahead of a matchup with Aaron Donald, fresh out of retirement.

Fifth-round rookie Carver Willis appears to be the favorite after veteran Robert Jones was released. Perhaps newly acquired lineman Jarrett Patterson will get a look, too, as Shanahan said he has the flexibility to play center or guard.

• Three receivers changed their jersey numbers. Jacob Cowing is now No. 4, De’Zhaun Stribling switched to No. 7, his high school number, and Demarcus Robinson chose No. 11, which was previously worn by Brandon Aiyuk.

Lynch said Aiyuk is not due to get any bonus money on Sept. 1 because he’s still on the reserve/left squad list. “He’s kind of not on our roster,” Lynch said.

• Right guard Dominick Puni, offensive tackle Vederian Lowe, quarterback Kurtis Rourke, fullback Kyle Juszczyk and safety Malik Mustapha were back at practice on Monday after missing time recently with injuries. Wide receiver Mike Evans, defensive tackle Gracen Halton, cornerback Renardo Green, linebacker Luke Gifford, Willis, Cowing and Hobbs worked on a side field. Bosa, Height and Prysock were not visible to reporters during the open portion of practice.

title: Deshaun Watson hasn't been good since 2020, why Browns still need a 2027 QB plan
description:
In other words, this wasn't merely an above-average season -- Watson was playing like one of the five best quarterbacks in football.
At this point, Watson doesn't have to become the 2020 version of himself for the comeback to be considered successful.
The Browns' 2027 QB isn't on the roster That brings the conversation to the bigger organizational question.
Cleveland's initial 53-man roster includes Watson, Sanders and sixth-round rookie Taylen Green, while Dillon Gabriel begins the season on injured reserve.
April still looks like the real decision point The Browns also shouldn't assume the 2027 draft will offer an easy answer.
text:
The Browns chose Deshaun Watson over Shedeur Sanders as their starting quarterback, a decision that answered the depth-chart question without ending the debate over who actually gives the team the best chance to win. First-year coach Todd Monken pointed to Watson's full body of work from the offseason, training camp, preseason games and joint practices as the reason, and he stressed that this was not intended to be a week-to-week decision. So that settles who gets the first opportunity, not whether Cleveland has found its answer at the position.

The much bigger question is whether Watson can be anything close to even an average NFL quarterback. The short answer, based on recent history, is no.

Watson's last elite season came in 2020, when he was 25 years old and still in Houston. Among 36 quarterbacks with at least 200 dropbacks that season, Watson ranked first in yards per attempt (8.9), second in passer rating (112.4), third in PFF passing grade (91.1) and third in positive-EPA rate (54.7%). His 0.24 EPA per dropback ranked fifth. In other words, this wasn't merely an above-average season -- Watson was playing like one of the five best quarterbacks in football. That player would solve Cleveland's quarterback problem immediately.

The problem is that version of Watson hasn't been seen in nearly six years.

* I know many of the metrics above have become commonplace in football discussions, but just in case, Positive EPA% basically answers the question, "How often did the offense end a pass play in a better scoring position than it started?"

The 2024 numbers are especially difficult to dismiss. Watson's -0.25 EPA per dropback was near the bottom of the league, his 37.8% positive-EPA rate was similarly poor, and he averaged only 5.3 yards per attempt. His 63.4 PFF passing grade was also well below the average of 72.6. Even before his last catastrophic injury, Watson wasn't playing like an average quarterback. He was playing like the least efficient quarterback in the league.

The layoff is long – the bigger problem is what came before it

Watson tore his right Achilles against Cincinnati on Oct. 20, 2024. He underwent surgery five days later, then re-ruptured the tendon during his recovery and required another surgery in January 2025. That setback wiped out his entire 2025 season.

If Watson starts Week 1 as expected, 693 days will have passed since his last regular-season appearance.

There are examples of quarterbacks returning after unusually long injury layoffs and having success. Some returned to essentially their previous levels, while others became functional starters again. But those comparisons become much more complicated with Watson.

*Bridgewater technically appeared before 2019, but 2019 was his first meaningful post-injury starting sample.

At first glance, that table might offer Cleveland some hope. Andrew Luck missed an entire season and returned as one of the NFL's best quarterbacks. Alex Smith essentially missed two years and still won games. Teddy Bridgewater eventually became a serviceable starter again. Dak Prescott and Joe Burrow came back from major lower-body injuries and were better afterward.

But those comparisons break down quickly when we start talking about Watson.

Watson isn't trying to return to where he left off

Most successful comeback quarterbacks were trying to regain a level of play they had demonstrated shortly before getting hurt.

Luck had posted a 90.3 PFF passing grade in his final full season before the lost year. Prescott had an 80.4 grade before his ankle injury. Burrow was already trending toward becoming a high-end starter before tearing his ACL. Even Smith, whose efficiency declined after his return, had been a competent NFL starter before suffering his devastating leg injury.

Watson isn't trying to get back to October 2024. He needs a time machine to take him back four years before that, to 2020. That's a completely different – and unprecedented – challenge.

Cleveland isn't dealing with one isolated injury that interrupted a productive career. Watson didn't play at all in 2021 after requesting a trade from Houston, spending the season inactive amid numerous civil lawsuits alleging sexual misconduct. After Cleveland traded for him, he missed the first 11 games of 2022 while serving an NFL suspension for violating the personal conduct policy, and then appeared in only six games that season. He played six more in 2023 before season-ending surgery on his throwing shoulder, then seven in 2024 before tearing his right Achilles. That same Achilles ruptured again during rehab, requiring a second surgery and ultimately costing him the entire 2025 season.

Over the five seasons since his last elite year, Watson has played 19 regular-season games. And when he has played, he hasn't been particularly good.

That makes the names in the table above much less reassuring. Cleveland isn't simply hoping that a 30-year-old quarterback can physically return after nearly two years away. It's hoping he can return from another prolonged absence and rediscover a level of production he hasn't shown since before the Browns traded for him.

At this point, Watson doesn't have to become the 2020 version of himself for the comeback to be considered successful. Simply becoming an average NFL quarterback would represent a substantial improvement from what Cleveland saw in those 19 games.

To repeat one of my favorite phrases when it comes to roster-building: Hope ain't a plan.

The Browns' 2027 QB isn't on the roster

That brings the conversation to the bigger organizational question.

Cleveland's initial 53-man roster includes Watson, Sanders and sixth-round rookie Taylen Green, while Dillon Gabriel begins the season on injured reserve. To varying degrees, there are reasons to continue developing the three young passers. There are not yet compelling reasons to believe any one of them should prevent Cleveland from drafting a quarterback in the first round next April.

Sanders is the most plausible internal candidate. He started seven games as a rookie and showed enough this summer to make the competition with Watson legitimate. But his 2025 season -- 56.6% completions, seven touchdowns, 10 interceptions, a 68.1 passer rating and an 18.9 QBR -- didn't provide anything close to a definitive answer.

And there is something revealing about the result of this summer's competition. Sanders couldn't beat out a quarterback returning from nearly two full seasons away who had played poorly the last time he was healthy.

That doesn't mean Sanders can't eventually become the answer. He may play this season and change the conversation entirely. But Cleveland shouldn't operate under the assumption that he will.

Gabriel started six games as a rookie and went 1-5 while averaging 5.1 yards per attempt. Green is a worthwhile developmental swing because of his size, athleticism and arm talent, and his 66 rushing yards in the preseason finale helped earn him a roster spot. Neither profile should stop Cleveland from pursuing a premium quarterback prospect if the opportunity presents itself.

April still looks like the real decision point

The Browns also shouldn't assume the 2027 draft will offer an easy answer. Every summer, the next QB class gets talked up as "loaded," and then the season has a way of telling a different story. Arch Manning and Dante Moore will draw plenty of attention, and there are other intriguing names, but this group could end up looking a lot more like 2025 or 2026 than the truly deep 2024 class that saw six QBs off the board in the first 12 picks. That doesn't change Cleveland's problem. It just makes the evaluation more important, because if the Browns are drafting a quarterback next April, they may have to identify the right one in a class with fewer sure things than advertised.

For now, Watson winning the Week 1 job obviously doesn't reset his career; instead, it gives him one last chance to prove he can still function as an NFL starter. Sanders is next in line based on how snaps were divvied up during training camp and the preseason. Gabriel, last year's third-round pick, appears to have lost standing with coach Kevin Stefanski gone, while Green is the developmental swing -- an athletic sixth-round rookie who isn't yet close to competing for a starting job.

Put another way: when you have four quarterbacks, you really have none. And Cleveland's schedule may force the issue quickly. The Browns open with two road games -- at Jacksonville, then at Tampa Bay against Baker Mayfield, the quarterback Cleveland effectively replaced with Watson in 2022 -- before finally returning home in Week 3 against Carolina.

Watson has already acknowledged how strained his relationship with the Browns faithful has become, saying that after being booed in the preseason, he feels more support on the road and noting that some fans cheered when he tore his Achilles in 2024.

He begins the season with an already tenuous hold on the job, and history isn't on his side. Two bad road starts could be enough to make the Week 3 home opener less of a celebration that football is back than a referendum on whether Watson has played his last snap for the Browns.

text:
NFL reps have not come easy for former Florida defensive lineman Caleb Banks, but he’s cleared his first hurdle: making the 53-man roster.

The deadline for NFL teams to cut their rosters down to 53 was Sunday. Banks survived the cuts and is slotted in as the starting nose tackle going into the Vikings’ Week 1 game against the Packers.

In two preseason games of action, Banks struggled, recording four tackles across 50 total snaps. Pro Football Focus gave him a grade of 30.4, placing him at the bottom of first-round rookies. In the second game, he improved but still produced a 48.1 overall grade.

“To be honest, I’m out of shape right now,” Banks said. “I need to run more gassers after practice; you guys will see me doing that.”

Drafted in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft in April, Banks had shown promise in his years at Florida; however, analysts had seen issues going in.

“His traits and flashes at the Senior Bowl make him an enticing prospect, but injury concerns are a potential stumbling block for him,” NFL analyst Lance Zierlein said in February.

At Florida, Banks played every game of his first two seasons, gaining a total of 40 tackles across both years. His 2024 season was especially notable, due to his 4.5 sacks and 7 tackles for loss. PFF graded that season at a 73.0 for Banks — second among Florida’s interior linemen that year behind Desmond Watson’s 75.4.

A nagging foot injury persisted before his senior season began, limiting him to three games. The ailment resurfaced in February at the NFL Scouting Combine, where he broke his foot, requiring surgery on March 9.

The Vikings have Banks slotted as the starting nose tackle in a base 3-4 scheme that blitzed 48% of the time in 2025, leading the league.

While Banks hasn’t played the best brand of football in the preseason, he showed enough promise for the defensive-minded coach, Brian Flores.

“I think we’ve got to give them time to really get their feet on the ground, literally on the field and figuratively, just as far as understanding the pro game, the routines, the habits that they’ve got to build to really reach their optimum potential,” Flores said.

text:
It should come as no surprise that the Miami Dolphins were awarded an NFL-high seven claims off the waiver wire.

That, after all, is the sign of team who needs to consistently churn the bottom of their roster in order to find gems.

Seven players — quarterback Brady Cook, defensive backs Reese Taylor, Marcellas Dial Jr. and Julius Wood; tackles Jarrett Kingston and Chukwuebuka Godrick; tight end Justin Joly — will soon find themselves in South Florida after Monday’s waiver wire claims went public. The Dolphins also signed defensive end Malik Herring to their active roster, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz.

Miami subsequently released edge Clelin Ferrell and cornerback A.J. Green III as well as ornerback Ethan Bonner, tackle Marques Cox, wide receiver AJ Henning, edge Max Llewellyn and offensive lineman Josh Priebe. Tight end Ben Sims was also waived with an injury designation.

Expect the Dolphins’ high number of waiver claims to be a trend this season, especially with the lack of established talent throughout the team’s 53-man roster.

“We owe it to this team and to the organization,” coach Jeff Hafley said during the final week of the preseason, adding that he and general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan “constantly have” conversations about the waiver wire. “If we feel like there are players out there that can help our roster, then we need to be aggressive. I know Sully and his entire staff, they’re working really hard on that. But that’s something that I think that we’re going to have to look at throughout the season as we look to move forward.”

A two-time Super Bowl champion with the Kansas City Chiefs, Herring provides depth and experience in the edge rusher room. He played his entire four-year career with the Chiefs, appearing in 28 games with one start, before joining the Tennessee Titans in the 2026 offseason and being waived ahead of the 53-man roster deadline. During his time in Kansas City, Herring accumulated 28 total tackles, 1.5 sacks and six quarterback hits.

Cook initially signed with the New York Jets as an undrafted free agent out of Missouri in April 2025. He would eventually appear in five games, four of which were starts, last season, racking up 739 yards and two touchdowns while completing roughly 58% of his passes. Cook also tossed seven picks during that span.

Taylor, who played cornerback, initially signed with the Denver Broncos’ practice squad in November 2023 after going undrafted. He has since fluctuated between the Broncos’ practice squad and active roster, appearing in five games — one in 2024, another in 2025 — and recording just two tackles across that span.

A sixth-round pick by the New England Patriots in 2024, Dial joins the Dolphins after appearing in all 17 games, starting one, as a rookie. The cornerback recorded 12 total tackles and a forced fumble before missing the entire 2025 season with a torn ACL in his left knee.

Wood arrives in Miami after spending the last season on the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad. In 2024, he appeared in nine games with the Tennessee Titans, racking up two tackles.

The San Francisco 49ers initially drafted Kingston in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft. He was waived after training camp and the Carolina Panthers would scoop him up. Kingston appeared in seven games for the Panthers at guard before being put on the team’s practice squad ahead of the 2025 season.

A month later, the Houston Texans would claim Kingston. He’d appear in two games with the Texans at tackle.

Godrick came to the Chiefs via the NFL’s International Player Path Program in 2023. He spent the majority of his time in Kansas City on the practice squad but appeared in four games, three of which were starts, at tackle.

The Broncos drafted Joly in the fifth round of 2026 NFL Draft. He started 34 games across his four years at North Carolina State (2024-25) and UConn (2022-23). Joly would end his collegiate career with 166 receptions for 1,978 yards and 15 touchdowns.

Nine players agreed to join the 16-member practice squad: quarterback Mark Gronowski, edge player Rodney McGraw, safety Major Burns, running backs Carlos Washington Jr. and Jarquez Hunter; offensive tackle Gottlieb Ayedze, tight end Jeremiah Franklin, receiver Jalen Reagor and linebacker Cam Riley.

Whether any of these players actually makes an impact remains to be seen.

title: Reds Get Encouraging Update on Elly De La Cruz After Injury Scare - Sports Illustrated
description:
The Cincinnati Reds appear to have avoided a significant injury with Elly De La Cruz.
De La Cruz left Sunday night’s game against the Chicago Cubs with left quad tightness, a concerning development considering it’s the same quad that gave him problems during the second half of last season.
No Reason to Play Him Tomorrow De La Cruz is a player that you sometimes need to save from himself.
However, the Reds are not making the postseason this year, and there is no reason to force De La Cruz back into the lineup on Monday.
If De La Cruz were to play Monday and aggravate the injury, the front office and Francona would be kicking themselves.
text:
The Cincinnati Reds appear to have avoided a significant injury with Elly De La Cruz.

De La Cruz left Sunday night’s game against the Chicago Cubs with left quad tightness, a concerning development considering it’s the same quad that gave him problems during the second half of last season.

Fortunately, the initial update from Reds manager Terry Francona was encouraging.

According to Charlie Goldsmith, Francona said after the game that he doesn’t believe the quad injury is very serious and there’s a chance De La Cruz could be back in the lineup as soon as Monday, when they face the Padres.

That certainly feels like the best-case scenario. De La Cruz is one of the most important players in Cincinnati’s lineup, and losing him for any extended period would be another major blow to an offense that has already struggled to consistently score runs.

Can't Always Trust Postgame Comments on Injuries

While it’s certainly an encouraging update, it’s also important to exercise some caution with a manager’s initial comments following a game.

When Reds outfielder/infielder Michael Toglia left a game a couple of weeks ago, Francona mentioned after the game that he thought Toglia had avoided serious injury and it sounded encouraging. Just two days later, the Reds announced that Toglia tore his labrum and would need season-ending surgery.

I am certainly not suggesting that is the case here, but the Reds will know more tomorrow.

No Reason to Play Him Tomorrow

De La Cruz is a player that you sometimes need to save from himself. He takes pride in being in the lineup every single day, and you have to applaud him for that. However, the Reds are not making the postseason this year, and there is no reason to force De La Cruz back into the lineup on Monday.

A day off would probably do him some good and, more importantly, give the Reds a chance to make sure he’s completely healthy.

If De La Cruz were to play Monday and aggravate the injury, the front office and Francona would be kicking themselves. At this point in the season, there is simply no reason to take that risk.

FLORHAM PARK, N.J. (AP) — Rookie Cade Klubnik will head into the regular season as the New York Jets' backup quarterback behind Geno Smith.

The fourth-rounder out of Clemson received the bulk of the snaps during the three preseason games and had a solid training camp performance, giving the Jets confidence he can step in Smith's place if needed.

"He's our backup quarterback," coach Aaron Glenn said Monday while announcing the decision. “And he'll do a good job.”

Glenn added that the Jets are still likely to add another quarterback to their practice squad. They released Bailey Zappe on Sunday. They also waived Brady Cook, who was claimed Monday by Miami. Cook started the final four games as a rookie last season.

Klubnik started the Jets' preseason opener against Tampa Bay and led New York to scores on his two drives. He came in after one series by Smith the following week at Pittsburgh and then played the first half of the preseason finale against the Giants.

Klubnik was 21 of 34 for 190 yards with no touchdowns and one interception in the three preseason games.

“There’s just a confidence in how he operates and what he’s done in practice, what he’s done in the games,” Glenn said. “I don’t think anybody ever said there weren’t going to be hiccups. I mean, he’s a rookie, but he’s always learning, he’s a very intelligent guy.”

“He's improved over the course of training camp, and he'll continue to improve."

Ossai will be sidelined a few weeks with a foot injury

Edge rusher Joseph Ossai will be “week to week,” according to Glenn, after he ruptured the plantar fascia in one of his feet against the Giants last Friday night.

Ossai, signed to a three-year, $36 million contract in March after five seasons with Cincinnati, began the summer on the physically unable to perform list and made his preseason debut against the Giants. He played 11 snaps and had two tackles and a quarterback pressure before being hurt.

Jets' kicking carousel continues to spin

New York claimed kicker Blake Grupe off waivers from Indianapolis on Monday, adding him to the roster after Jason Sanders — who beat out Cade York for the job — had a shaky performance in the preseason finale during which he was wide left on an extra point and short on a 54-yard field-goal attempt.

Sanders was released by the Jets a few hours after Glenn said the veteran remained on the team for “competition” with Grupe while adding that the roster is still “fluid” as teams continue to make moves in preparation for the regular season. Sanders was later re-signed — but to the practice squad.

New York also claimed former Carolina linebacker Trevin Wallace and waived offensive lineman Kohl Levao.

Grupe spent parts of his first three NFL seasons with New Orleans and finished last year with the Colts, who waived him Sunday after Spencer Shrader won their competition. For his career, Grupe is 86 of 105 on field goals and 96 of 98 on extra points.

“He's a small guy,” the 5-foot-9 Glenn said with a laugh about the 5-7 Grupe. “But he’s a good player. ... Looking forward to him getting out here with us and kicking.”

text:
The grim reaper has taken the NFL by storm throughout August. Players are now hurt, and we must figure out what to do about it. The rankings have shifted, and if you have not yet drafted, changes must account for them. On the other hand, if you have drafted, we have some useful advice to share. Here are the latest injuries to be advised about.

Pat Mahomes

The Chiefs quarterback is going to be a full-go for Week 1. His rushing upside will be limited, but Mahomes does expect to still scramble in low-risk scenarios. He is still a mild risk and is only ranked around QB12 in fantasy football. Draft a backup for safekeeping.

Jeremiyah Love

Love is still about a 50/50 shot to play Week 1. He will have a multi-week ramp-up to full health. Despite the ankle sprain, he is at low risk long-term. I am below consensus, favoring Tyler Allgeier to get 25-30% of the rushing offense, but I do not hate drafting Love in the 4th or 5th round.

Chuba Hubbard

The Panthers are trending towards having Hubbard back for Week 1. While probably not 100%, his playing time should not see much of a dip. Hubbard is expected to have a 60/40 split over Jonathan Brooks. Both are lower-risk draft picks in a run-favoring offense.

Kyle Monangai

D'Andre Swift is going to have the early advantage in Chicago. While Monangai earned his 50/50 split in 2025, early-season woes could give Swift formidable volume well into the season. Monangai is uncertain to play Week 1 and will require a multi-week ramp-up from his knee hyperextension. Monangai sits around RB40 while Swift is around RB20, also with lower injury risk.

Kenneth Walker III

The cited foot issue is not expected to sideline Walker or limit him. He will play Week 1, backed up by Emmett Johnson, who earned the RB2 job and is a prime handcuff.

Ashton Jeanty

It has been reported that Jeanty has a mild high-ankle sprain. Nothing has technically been confirmed on that matter. Suffering last week, Jeanty will truly be on the brink of a return for Week 1. He is in questionable status but hopes to be ready by Week 2 and mostly back to form by Week 4 at the latest. Mike Washington Jr. will be very capable if Jeanty is out; a low-end RB2. I would still draft Jeanty around RB9-12 off the board.

TreVeyon Henderson

Despite an ankle injury, Henderson is expected to play Week 1. He is my low-risk RB24.

Alvin Kamara

The Saints notably kept Kamara off the IR. This means he can return at any time before Week 4. Kamara has been reported missing for about one month. With nearly two weeks until Week 1 and a week removed from injury, a Week 2 or 3 return is most likely.

Breece Hall

Hall's sidelining due to a groin injury has been especially precautionary. He should be a full-go for Week 1.

Zach Charbonnet

My continuous take on Charbonnet has come true. As many fans had hoped for Charbonnet's early-season return, the Seahawks did place him on the IR. Charbonnet should not return until at least October, and would not be close to 100% until the final third of the season.

Alec Pierce

The Colts finally got Pierce back to practice this past week. He appears to look quite good considering his muscle atrophy concerns. It will now be up to Pierce to get in game shape, and if all looks good on the field, Pierce can definitely be a WR2. As of now, he is a low-end WR3 with moderate re-injury risk, so I will not draft Pierce at anything higher than my fourth wide receiver; a high-upside depth piece.

Malik Nabers

Nabers looks fresh, is cutting very well, and is now primed to play Week 1, well ahead of schedule. Nabers can be drafted in the WR12-15 range. There is a mild re-injury risk.

Emeka Egbuka

It is not great to hear Todd Bowles say he is "hopeful" that Egbuka is good for Week 1. Egbuka is projected as my WR26, but I would exercise some caution and wait until the WR30-33 range to pull the trigger. Chris Godwin's stock rises in the meantime; low-risk and high-upside or a great mid-round wide receiver prospect.

Puka Nacua

Nacua is back practicing after his psoas limited him on the field. All reports point towards a full-go Nacua in Week 1, and he is well worth his top-2 wide receiver status. Nacua also avoided the Commissioners Exemption List and is not expected to be suspended.

Ja'Marr Chase

Chase has a bone bruise from knee hyperextension. He will be sidelined for a couple of weeks, but is expected to be quite fine for the Bengals opener. Do not panic at all and make the pick with clarity.

Mike Evans

The 49ers expect Evans to play in Week 1. I am very worried about placing Evans on my fantasy football team. He has continuous issues with his hamstring and groin that will likely persist throughout the season. Evans only played 8 games in 2025.

Luther Burden III

The Bears have always expected his Week 1 return, and with zero setbacks, Burden III is well worth his ADP.

Sam LaPorta

It sounds like LaPorta had a very minor hip bruise. He will be just fine for Week 1, primed for a big comeback season under Drew Petzing. I doubt this is a Trey McBride in the making, but LaPorta is definitely a top-10 tight end with top-6 upside.

Tucker Kraft

Kraft recently retracted statements that he might be on a minor snap count. 2026 should have big things in store for Kraft, who was a TE2 pre-injury in 2025.

Tyler Warren

Warren has been dealing with a minor groin injury, but there is no concern for his Week 1 status.

George Kittle

It is still not clear if Kittle will make the trip to play in Week 1 in Australia. I would lean toward him doing so based on reporting, but I have a backup plan. Personally, I rank Kittle as my TE15 and would not draft him without another member of the supporting cast.

Brosmer started two games for the Vikings last season. After former starter J.J. McCarthy and then-backup Carson Wentz suffered injuries, Minnesota turned to the undrafted rookie from the University of Minnesota earlier than the team had planned. Brosmer began his career with four interceptions against the Seattle Seahawks but contributed to a win at MetLife Stadium against the New York Giants three weeks later.

As of Monday evening, the Vikings still had three quarterbacks on the roster: starter Kyler Murray, Wentz and McCarthy. Coach Kevin O’Connell has not yet clarified the depth chart, though several team sources, speaking on condition of anonymity to discuss internal team matters, said they expect Wentz to become the backup. This leaves McCarthy, a first-round pick in 2024, in a murky situation, especially considering his most recent injury.

The 23-year-old missed Friday’s final preseason game against the Broncos with an ankle injury. At the time, team sources said McCarthy did not feel comfortable playing in the game, but that the injury was “minor.” ESPN’s Adam Schefter told “The Pat McAfee Show” on Monday that he thinks McCarthy’s ankle “is a multi-week injury.”

To this point, the Vikings have not placed McCarthy on injured reserve, a move that could have allowed the team to keep another young talent — like Brosmer — on the roster.

Already dealing with familiar injury volume, the 49ers used both their IR-return slots upon setting their initial 53-man roster Sunday. The team added two more IR-return players today.

Cornerback Nate Hobbs and linebacker Nick Martin are heading to IR, per the team. Safety Ashtyn Davis and punter Corliss Waitman, whom the 49ers released Sunday, are coming back in corresponding moves.

Hobbs is dealing with a groin issue, while Martin suffered a hamstring injury in the 49ers’ second preseason game. Both players are expected to return sometime during the season, according to Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area. The 49ers previously gave return designations to wide receiver Christian Kirk and tackle Austen Pleasants. Teams are only allowed to designate eight players to return from IR during the season.

Hobbs put together a 16-game rookie season with the Raiders in 2021, but injuries have been a frequent occurrence since then. He missed between four and six games in each of his last three seasons with the Raiders. Despite that, the Packers gave Hobbs a four-year, $48MM contract in free agency in 2025. It did not go well for the Pack, who saw Hobbs miss six games with knee problems. Over 11 games (five starts) and 358 defensive snaps, Hobbs totaled 27 tackles and a mere two pass breakups.

Green Bay released Hobbs in March, but it only took the 27-year-old two days to land an opportunity in San Francisco. The 49ers guaranteed Hobbs $3.11MM on a one-year, $3.5MM pact, though it looks as if it will be a while before he contributes (if he does). As things stand, Deommodore Lenoir, Renardo Green, Upton Stout, free agent addition Jack Jones and fourth-round rookie Ephesians Prysock make up the 49ers’ top five corners.

Martin, a 2025 third-rounder from Oklahoma State, got into seven games as a rookie and made 11 tackles before a concussion ended his season in December. Martin will continue to miss time at the start of 2026 as a result of his latest injury, but the 49ers are deep enough at linebacker to get by without him. Superstar Fred Warner is healthy again after missing most of last season with an ankle injury, and the team reunited with Dre Greenlaw in free agency. The 49ers have fifth-round rookie/summer standout Jaden Dugger, Tatum Bethune, special teams ace Luke Gifford and Garrett Wallow behind Warner and Greenlaw.

Connor Byrne contributed to this post.
